text.p: Stock prices fell sharply in early trading Friday, capping a week of strong volatility amid a slew of benign inflation reports.

At 10 a.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 107.31 points, or 1.3 percent, at 7,834.72 after a drop of 50 points minutes after the opening activated the New York Stock Exchange's limits on program trading.
The Nasdaq composite index was down 9.12 points at 1,577.57.

The bond market was also lower, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond sliding a full point, which raised its yield to 6.63 percent from Thursday's close of 6.55 percent. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
The expiration of stock options and stock index options added to the market's volatility.
On Thursday, the blue-chip index swung erratically from the plus to the minus column, and settled with a 14-point gain.
Analysts said the market still needed to consolidate after its strong run up in recent weeks despite the current good outlook for inflation.
"In between we are just looking at a Friday in August and I see a bit of a void," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities.

This week, the government reported more good news on inflation with the Producer Price Index falling 0.1 percent for a record seventh straight month in July and the Consumer Price Index inching up just 0.2 percent.
Among individual issues, W.R.Grace rose 7/8 at 70-3/8 after announcing late Thursday that it would sell its packaging unit to Sealed Air in a deal valued at $5 billion.
